title: Room booking service in Java
idea: BookingService is a facade: one `book` call filters free rooms through each Calendar, asks a RoomSelectionStrategy to pick one, stores the Booking, and notifies a listener.

analogy.text: A front desk clerk. You state a time and headcount; the clerk checks each room's sheet, follows the house rule for choosing, and phones you back.
analogy.breaks: Changing the house rule here means plugging in a new class.

points: Facade: callers know only `book`, not calendars, strategies or listeners.
Strategy: RoomSelectionStrategy decides which free room wins; it is injected.
Observer: a BookingListener hears about confirmed bookings, for email or chat.
A new policy is a new class; BookingService itself never changes.

hero.title: One book() call, stage by stage

steps.caption: E-2 asks for a room for three people from 10:30 to 11:30.
Every room's Calendar answers `isFree`. Orion already holds BK-1 from 10:00, so it drops out.
The injected strategy picks the smallest room that fits. Lyra seats six, Vega ten.
The service creates BK-2 and adds it to Lyra's Calendar only.
Listeners hear about the confirmed booking. Email or chat code lives outside the service.
The Booking returns to the caller. With no fitting room, the strategy returns empty instead.

code.title: Core flow
code.caption: The facade, the default strategy and a listener, booking four requests against three rooms.

walk.text: Three rooms, the smallest-fit strategy and a listener that prints notifications.
Four requests: a fit, a conflict, a group too large, and back-to-back.
The strategy interface and its default: smallest capacity that fits, then by id.
A Calendar per room answers `isFree` with the half-open overlap rule.
Dependencies come in through the constructor, so tests can swap them.
Filter free rooms, then let the strategy choose; empty means no room.
Store the Booking in that room's Calendar, then tell the listener.

code.title: New strategy, no edits
code.caption: The same free rooms ranked by two policies. The second is a new class; nothing old is edited.

walk.text: Three free rooms and two policies; the organizer sits on floor 5.
Run each policy on the same input and print its pick.
NearestFloorStrategy ranks by distance from the organizer's floor, then by capacity.

pitfalls: Do not branch on policy names inside BookingService; inject a RoomSelectionStrategy.
Listeners run inside `book`, so a slow mail server blocks it; listeners should only queue.
Return an empty result for no room; null hides the failure from callers.

quiz.q: What does NearestFloor print for NearestFloorStrategy?
quiz.why: The organizer is on floor 5. Lyra is on floor 5, distance zero, and seats six, so it beats both floor 3 rooms.

takeaway: One facade call; swappable choice policy; notifications through listeners.

starters: Why is the listener an interface instead of a direct email call?
How would I combine two strategies, such as nearest floor then smallest?
Where should the room lock go when this runs on many threads?
